land.text: Khwarazm, where 'in 1511 his garrison was expelled and power passed to Ilbars'

predecessors.note: The Khiva page lists the Timurid Empire as its predecessor; the Shaybanids held Khwarazm 1505-1510 and a Safavid garrison until 1511 (Khiva page: Khorezm 'shortly occupied' after Merv).

land.text: the Khiva oasis: Khorezm and the Tashauz (Dashoguz) bank of the Amu Darya delta

successors.note: Declared by the First Khorezm Kurultay on 26 April 1920; a state Cliopatria lacks, not in the owned list (see the report).

capitals.name: Khiva
capitals.note: 'Some time around 1600, the Daryaliq or west branch of the Oxus dried up causing the capital to be moved south to Khiva'; another passage credits Arap Muhammad (1602-23).

rulers.name: Ilbars I
rulers.note: 'Ilbars, who founded the long-lived Arabshahid dynasty'; reign 1511-1518 on the page.

rulers.name: Sultan Haji
rulers.note: Short reign; real power lay with his cousin Sultan Ghazi.

rulers.name: Muhammad Amin Biy (Inaq)
rulers.title: inaq (regent of puppet khans)
rulers.note: The page also gives 'Muhammed Amin (1755-1782)' in its inaq list.

rulers.name: Eltuzar (Iltuzar) Khan
rulers.note: 'formalized as the Qongrat dynasty by Iltuzar Khan in 1804'; he died after a failed raid on Bukhara. His end year is taken from Muhammad Rahim's accession.

rulers.name: Allah Quli Khan
rulers.note: The lead of the Khiva page gives 1825-1840.

correction.text: Khwarazm as in the 1512 shape, the Arabshahid state of Ilbars I

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1511: the infobox says 'Established: 1511'; 'in 1511 his garrison was expelled and power passed to Ilbars'. Cliopatria starts the row at 1512.
87,272 km2 for 1512-1520: the Khorezm oasis. The infobox gives 67,521 km2 for 1911 (after the 1873 losses), so the 16th-century oasis figure is the right order.

125,454 km2 for 1521-1587: the oasis plus 125 cells of the delta and Aral shore to the north (no page dates them; the page has Karakalpaks 'increasingly' filling the delta). Ratio to the 1911 infobox 1.9: within the factor of two. The Bukharan incursions of 1538 and 1593 are occupations in the ledger and do not change the shape.
125,257 km2 for 1588-1717: unchanged. The capital moves to Khiva about 1600 (infobox: Khiva from 1599).
125,454 km2 for 1718-1720: unchanged. The Bekovich-Cherkassky expedition of 1717 'attacked Khiva and was soundly defeated'.
125,563 km2 for 1721-1737: unchanged (a few cells of the desert edge).

125,257 km2 for 1738-1747: the oasis. Nader Shah 'conquered the Khanate of Khiva' in 1740 and 'beheaded Ilbars'; the Afsharid occupation runs 1740-1746/47 (Khiva page). An occupation in the ledger, not a change of shape.

334,102 km2 for 1748-1751: the oasis plus 720 cells of the Kyzylkum (taken from Bukhara's shape) and the northern Karakum. Unverified: page budget. The Khiva page says only that after 1746 'the Qongrat tribe became increasingly powerful' and that Khiva regained independence after Nader's death in 1747 (Nader Shah page).
334,312 km2 for 1752-1790: unchanged. Unverified: page budget. The Inaq period (Muhammad Amin Biy 1763-1790) runs through it.

738,496 km2 for 1791-1796: 1,385 cells added - the Turkmen lands to the Caspian shore (Balkanabat, Turkmenbashi, Ashgabat, Tejen) and the Ustyurt/Aral steppe to 46.3 N. Unverified: page budget; no opened page dates or maps this expansion (Avaz Inaq 1790-1804 on the Khiva page, whose own article could not be opened). A claimed sphere over nomads rather than administered land; ratio to the 1911 infobox 10.9.
738,446 km2 for 1797-1799: unchanged. Unverified: page budget.

738,422 km2 for 1800-1821: unchanged. Muhammad Rahim I 'finally subdued the Uzbek tribes of the Amu Darya delta who had broken away' in 1811 and 'subdued the Kazakh tribes of the lower Syr Darya' in 1812-1813; the Qongrat dynasty was formalized in 1804 (Khiva page).

847,836 km2 for 1822-1855: 434 cells added around Merv and the Karakum south to 35.3 N, 49 cells of the lower Syr Darya steppe dropped. The Merv page: 1823: Control of Merv passed to the Khanate of Khiva; Muhammad Rahim I 'conquered the city of Merv' in the 1820s (Rahim page): the shape is one year early. Ratio to the 1911 infobox 12.6: Cliopatria draws the claimed Turkmen sphere, which the 1911 settled khanate (after the 1856 loss of Merv and 1873) does not match. The 1840 Perovsky expedition failed and changed nothing.

correction.text: the 1856 shape without the Merv oasis, where the Tekke Turkmen were sovereign from about 1856

keyframe_review.note: 848,154 km2 for 1856: still holds the Merv oasis. The Merv page: c. 1856: The Tekke Turkmen became the sovereign power in the area and held it until the Russians occupied the oasis in 1884; the Khiva page has 'a long Turkmen rebellion (1855-1867)' and its khan list ends Muhammad Amin on 19 March 1855.

correction.text: the 1857 shape without the Merv oasis, Tekke Turkmen land

keyframe_review.note: 848,279 km2 for 1857-1863: the same Merv correction.

correction.text: the 1864 shape without the Merv oasis

keyframe_review.note: 384,765 km2 for 1864-1872: 1,579 cells fewer than 1857 (the Caspian Turkmen coast and the Ustyurt/Aral steppe go; no opened page dates it - the Khiva page has the Turkmen rebellion 1855-1867 and a Russian fort on the Aral from 1848). Merv removed as above. Ratio to the 1911 infobox 5.7: still the claimed Karakum sphere (the Khorezm oasis proper is about 70,000 km2).

correction.text: the khanate after 1873: the Khiva oasis, 'a quasi-independent Russian protectorate' with an area of 67,521 km2 in 1911

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1873-1917, which Cliopatria leaves without a Khiva row: Khiva 'remained a Russian protectorate until the revolution' (Khivan campaign page). The Amu Darya Division was annexed from Khiva in 1873 (Russian Turkestan page) and a strip went to Bukhara in October 1873. What is left is the oasis: infobox area 67,521 km2 (1911); the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic of 1920 had 62,200 km2. Khorezm plus Tashauz is 69,000 km2 on the grid. The Russian Empire dossier should draw this land as a vassal tint.

correction.text: the Khiva oasis, 62,200 km2 in the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic of 1920

keyframe_review.note: 384,765 km2 (the 1864 shape again) for 1918: five times the infobox area for 1911 and still including Merv, long Russian since 1884. The khanate of 1918 is the 1873 remnant; the khan Sayid Abdullah abdicated on 2 February 1920 (Khiva page).
384,765 km2 for 1919: the same error as 1918.

New keyframe for January-February 1920: the khanate ends on 2 February 1920 and the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic (62,200 km2; capital Khiva) is declared on 26 April 1920 - a successor row Cliopatria lacks.

ledger.note: 1511: Ilbars expels the Safavid garrison and founds the Arabshahid state at Urgench. The Khanate of Khiva page: after the battle near Merv in 1510 'Khorezm [was] shortly occupied' by Shah Ismail I; 'The Shah's religion provoked resistance and in 1511 his garrison was expelled and power passed to Ilbars, who founded the long-lived Arabshahid dynasty'; infobox 'Established: 1511'. (Reviewer ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: counterpart was shaybanids.)

region.text: the delta and the Aral shore, 125 cells north of the oasis

ledger.note: 1521: the Amu Darya delta and the Aral shore enter Cliopatria's shape. No page dates it; 'the swampy area of the lower delta was increasingly populated by Karakalpaks'.

1538: Ubaydullah Khan of Bukhara enters Khwarazm. He killed the local Khan Avanish and was driven out by Din Muhammad; the Khiva page dates Bukharan wars to '1538-40' and the Khans 'driven out by the Bukharans' around 1540.
1538-39: Din Muhammad drives the Bukharans out; Ubaydullah dies in 1539. The page does not date the expulsion.

1593-94: Abdullah Khan II of Bukhara occupies Khwarazm. His troops conquered Khwarazm. He marched on Khiva, where the local sultans were captured and executed. The Khiva page: 'Around 1540 and 1593, the Khans were driven out by the Bukharans.'
1598: Abdullah Khan II dies and the Bukharan hold lapses. No opened page says when the Arabshahids returned; Arap Muhammad is khan 1602-1623 on the Khiva page.
1599: the capital moves from Konye-Urgench to Khiva. Infobox: 'Konye-Urgench (1511-1598), Khiva (1599-1920)'; 'Some time around 1600, the Daryaliq or west branch of the Oxus dried up'.

1740: Nader Shah conquers Khiva. 'In 1740, he conquered the Khanate of Khiva' and, on the Khiva page, 'conquered Khiva, beheaded Ilbars and freed some 12,000-20,000 slaves'; the infobox calls it a vassal state of Afsharid Iran 1740-1747 and the lead an occupation 1740-1746.

1747: Nader Shah is murdered and Khiva is free: 'Oman and the Uzbek khanates of Bukhara and Khiva regained independence'. The Khiva page puts the Afsharid occupation at 1740-1746 in its lead and 1747 in its status line.

region.text: the Kyzylkum fringe held by Bukhara's 1738 shape and Khiva's 1748 shape

ledger.note: 1748: the Kyzylkum fringe north-west of Bukhara enters Khiva's shape. No opened page dates it or names the land; the Qongrat tribe 'became increasingly powerful' after 1746.

region.text: the desert south and west of the oasis added in Cliopatria's 1748 shape

ledger.note: 1748: the northern Karakum steppe enters Khiva's shape; no opened page dates it. Nothing marks the land as a state's.

region.text: Turkmen lands to the Caspian shore and the Ustyurt steppe

ledger.note: 1791: the Turkmen coast and the Ustyurt/Aral steppe enter Khiva's shape - 1,385 cells to 46.3 N and the Caspian. Under Avaz Inaq (1790-1804, Khiva page) but the page names no conquest; a claimed nomad sphere. Unverified: page budget.

1804: the Qongrat dynasty is formalized under Iltuzar Khan. 'After 1746, the Qongrat tribe became increasingly powerful and appointed puppet khans'; 'Their power was formalized as the Qongrat dynasty by Iltuzar Khan in 1804.' The Arabshahid line ends; the state continues.

1811: Muhammad Rahim Khan I recovers the delta. 'In 1811, he finally subdued the Uzbek tribes of the Amu Darya delta who had broken away from Khiva.' Cliopatria already draws the delta inside the khanate; the Karakalpakstan reading is the researcher's.

region.text: the lower Syr Darya, where 'He also subdued the Kazakh tribes of the lower Syr Darya in 1812-1813'

ledger.note: 1812-1813: the lower Syr Darya Kazakhs are subdued ('He subdued the Kazakh tribes of the lower Syr Darya'). The page gives 1812-1813; the year is the span's end. Cliopatria's Khiva shape drops the lower Syr Darya in 1822. (Reviewer ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: region was the whole Qyzylorda province, 422 of its 741 cells outside every Khiva shape and never lost again; now the lower Syr Darya inside Cliopatria's 1800 shape, as for the 1811 delta event.)

1823: Merv comes to Khiva. 'Control of Merv passed to the Khanate of Khiva'; Muhammad Rahim I 'conquered the city of Merv' in the 1820s (Rahim page). The page does not name the previous holder: Cliopatria's Emirate of Bukhara shape holds Merv 1800-1821, after Shah Murad razed it in 1788-89.

c. 1856: the Tekke Turkmen take Merv. 'The Tekke Turkmen became the sovereign power in the area and held it until the Russians occupied the oasis in 1884'; Khiva's 'long Turkmen rebellion (1855-1867)'.

region.text: Turkmen coast, Ustyurt and Aral steppe

ledger.note: 1864: the Caspian Turkmen coast and the Ustyurt/Aral steppe leave Cliopatria's shape (1,579 cells). No opened page dates it; the Turkmen rebellion ran 1855-1867 and a Russian fort stood on the Aral from 1848.

region.text: the Khiva oasis: Khorezm and the Tashauz (Dashoguz) bank of the Amu Darya delta

ledger.note: 11 March 1873: the Russian columns set out. 'The Aralsk force set out on 11 March 1873', Kaufmann left Jizzakh on 23 March; the Orenburg and Lomakin forces joined on 24 May. The page gives march dates, not the first ground held.

region.text: the Khiva oasis: Khorezm and the Tashauz (Dashoguz) bank of the Amu Darya delta

ledger.note: 14 June 1873: Khiva falls. Kaufmann entered the city after the khan surrendered on the night of 9-10 June and the Khan was reinstated on June 14 (infobox: campaign '11 March - 14 June 1873').

region.text: the Amu Darya Division, annexed from the khanate

ledger.note: 24 August 1873 (12 August old style): Khiva cedes the Amu Darya Division and becomes a Russian protectorate. 'To these were added in 1873 the Amu Darya Division', annexed from Khiva; 'on 12 August 1873, a peace treaty was signed that established Khiva as a quasi-independent Russian protectorate' (Khiva page), 'On August 24 ... a treaty was signed' (campaign page). The pages do not give the division's extent or the bank of the river; Karakalpakstan is the researcher's reading. A garrison stood at Petroalexandrovsk.

region.text: a strip of Khivan land along the Bukharan border

ledger.note: October 1873: a strip of Khivan territory went to Bukhara as a reward for the Amir's neutrality. The page does not locate it; the band along the Khiva-Bukhara border is the researcher's placeholder.

2 February 1920: the last khan abdicates and the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic follows. 'On 2 February 1920, Khiva's last Kungrad khan, Sayid Abdullah, abdicated'; the First Khorezm Kurultay declared the republic on 26 April 1920 (62,200 km2).

wars.name: Bukharan wars against Khwarazm
wars.outcome: Ubaydullah Khan kills the khan Avanish in 1538 and is driven out; the Khiva page dates Bukharan wars to '1538-40'.

wars.name: Abdullah Khan II's conquest of Khwarazm
wars.outcome: The sultans of Khiva are captured and executed; the Bukharan hold lapses after 1598.

wars.name: Bekovich-Cherkassky expedition
wars.outcome: The Russian expedition 'attacked Khiva and was soundly defeated', only a few men escaping.
wars.note: The Khivan campaign of 1839 page mentions it in passing; no dedicated article was opened.

wars.name: Nader Shah's conquest of Khiva
wars.outcome: Nader conquers Khiva, beheads Ilbars and frees 12,000-20,000 slaves; Khiva is an Afsharid vassal or occupied territory until 1746/47.

wars.name: Russian expedition against Khiva (Perovsky)
wars.outcome: 10 October 1839 to June 1840: the Russian column of 5,000 retreats on 13 February 1840 after losing 1,054 men; the aim was a loyal Kazakh khan, not annexation.

wars.name: Turkmen rebellion against Khiva

zones.text: Merv, where the Tekke were sovereign from about 1856

wars.outcome: 'A long Turkmen rebellion (1855-1867)'; Merv is lost about 1856.
wars.note: The Merv page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merv) gives c. 1856 for the Tekke; the Yomut opposed Khiva's irrigation and tax reforms.

wars.name: Khivan campaign of 1873
wars.outcome: Russian columns converge on Khiva (11 March - 14 June 1873); the khan surrenders on 9-10 June and is reinstated on 14 June; a treaty of 24 August 1873 makes Khiva a protectorate, abolishes slavery, opens the Oxus to Russian boats and sets an indemnity of 2,200,000 roubles payable until 1893; the Amu Darya Division is annexed and a strip goes to Bukhara.
wars.note: Treaty of Gandemian and the Amu Darya Division pages could not be opened (404); the Russian Turkestan and Khiva pages give 1873.

certainty.note: Oasis frontiers against Turkmen and Kazakh nomads and the Karakum; Cliopatria's large 1791-1863 shapes are claimed spheres, not administered land.
The August 1873 treaty ceded the Amu Darya Division, but no opened page gives the line; the remaining frontier is the oasis edge and the Amu Darya.

notes:
Khanate of Khiva: 1511..1920 (Cliopatria 1512..1919, 17 shapes, none for 1873-1917). Pages opened: 9 for the budget (Khiva, Nader Shah, Khivan campaign of 1873, Russian conquest of Central Asia, Russian Turkestan, Muhammad Rahim Khan I, Khorezm People's Soviet Republic, Merv, Khivan campaign of 1839), plus Ubaydullah Khan and Abdullah Khan II shared with the Bukhara dossier. Failed pages (404): Treaty of Gandemian, Amu Darya Division, Avaz Inaq, a Wikipedia search URL.
Cliopatria problems and decisions:
- No row 1873-1917 although the khanate lived on as a protectorate: new keyframe khanate-of-khiva_1873 (Khorezm + Tashauz, 69,000 km2 on the grid against the infobox 67,521 km2 for 1911). The Russian Empire dossier (eu-17) should record vassal_start (12/24 August 1873) and vassal_end (February 1920) for khanate-of-khiva; a protectorate has no event type in the vassal's own dossier.
- The 1918 and 1919 rows are the 1864 shape (384,765 km2, with Merv) and are wrong; replaced by the oasis.
- Merv: Cliopatria keeps it 1822-1872; pages put it with Khiva 1823-c.1856 and Tekke Turkmen afterwards; removed from 1856.
- The large 1791-1863 shapes (738,000 to 848,000 km2) are claimed spheres over Turkmen and Kazakh nomads; no opened page dates the 1748, 1791 or 1864 changes (verdict ok, 'unverified: page budget', events at confidence 1).
- Afsharid occupation 1740-1746/47: the Khiva page's infobox says vassal, its lead says occupation; recorded as occupation (the afsharid-iran dossier owns the matching event).
- 1873 date: 12 August (Khiva page, old style) and 24 August (campaign page, new style) are the same treaty.
Counterparts without a dossier: khorezm-people-s-soviet-republic (1920-1924, successor), Tekke Turkmen (Merv, c.1856-1884; a confederation rather than a state).
Region names the gazetteer lacks: none needed (Khorezm, Tashauz, Margiana, Karakalpakstan, Qyzylorda resolve). The Amu Darya Division's extent is the researcher's reading.
